claims.hypothesis: Does disk-scale dust polarization trace magnetic fields?
claims.experiment: 1.3 mm full-polarization survey of 28 fields with morphology/inclination/beta analysis
claims.finding: Polarization mostly reflects self-scattering in optically thick disks, not magnetic fields

evidence.quote: the majority (9/14) of the detected sources have polarization morphologies and disk properties consistent with dust self-scattering processes in optically thick disks.

claims.hypothesis: Inclination controls polarization morphology and detectability
claims.experiment: Compare inclinations of detected vs undetected sources (Anderson-Darling)

evidence.quote: We find that the sources with uniform polarization tend to have steeper inclinations ($> 60$) than those with azimuthal polarization ($< 60$).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: k-RAT, aerodynamic alignment, mechanical torques not favoured for uniform sources

evidence.quote: we do not favour any of these alternative polarization mechanisms for our sources with uniform polarization angles.

limitations_admitted.value: Gaussian fits and masses are approximate; inclinations biased for compact disks; dust scattering effects on beta ignored

evidence.quote: We caution, however, that both the Gaussian fits and the mass measurements should be considered approximations
